coach.name: George Halcovage III
coach.since: 2023 (hired from Villanova, where he was associate head coach); 2026-27 is his fourth season
coach.notes: Hired 2023 after 15 seasons as a Villanova assistant (worked with Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges). Year one: 4-27 (2-16 MAC); 2025-26: 17-15 (7-11 MAC), a 13-win improvement; entered 2026-27 at 30-64 overall, 13-41 MAC. Contract extended through 2029-30; original deal averaged $445,000/yr, extension terms undisclosed (Spectrum, Sep. 16, 2026). Says UB 'didn't have the depth to sustain some injuries' late last season and that expectations have shifted to competing for the MAC. The 716 Club NIL/revenue-share collective launched July 2026 with $500,000 in commitments. 2025-26 defense ranked 22nd percentile nationally per CBB Analytics (Mid-Major Basketball).

previews.title: 2026-27 Mid-American Men's Basketball Overview
previews.author: Kaily "KG" Godek (Buffalo section) and Foster Roesti
previews.summary: Buffalo lost its top six scorers and returns no starters from the 17-15 team. Halcovage rebuilt from multiple levels, adding eight former NCAA Division I players plus D-III and NAIA standouts. Syracuse transfer J.J. Starling is called the key portal pickup, and NIU transfer Dylan Ducommun brings MAC experience. The piece says chemistry may take time but calls Buffalo a potential conference surprise depending on how it develops.

previews.title: Coach George Halcovage III turned men's basketball from 4-27 to 17-15. He's far from done
previews.author: Will Meyer
previews.summary: Senior sports editor Will Meyer profiles Halcovage entering year four after taking UB from 4-27 to 17-15. Halcovage calls last season a 'proof of concept' for UB's roster-building and development model, notes his contract runs through 2029-30, and says increased financial support (the 716 Club launched in July with $500,000 in commitments) is the program's biggest improvement, though UB is 'not exactly in the spot we want to be yet' on NIL. UB must replace departed stars Ryan Sabol and Daniel Freitag; J.J. Starling was awaiting an eligibility decision on a fifth season at publication. Halcovage: 'The best guards are the toughest guards.' Expectations shift from showing progress to competing for a MAC title.

player_claims.claim: Baldwinsville native, former five-star at Notre Dame/Syracuse; awaiting a decision on eligibility for a fifth collegiate season as of Sep. 16; Halcovage says he wants to help UB 'compete to win a MAC championship.'

previews.title: Buffalo: Fast start fades as inconsistency, transfers shape uncertain future
previews.author: Logan Weingartner
previews.summary: Offseason look-ahead after Buffalo's 17-15 season and MAC quarterfinal loss to Akron. The Bulls started 13-2, then lost seven of their next 10, with defense ranking in the 22nd percentile nationally. Top scorers Daniel Freitag (Oregon State) and Ryan Sabol (Providence) left via the portal, Angelo Brizzi entered the portal and center Tim Oboh committed to Penn State. Guard Jahrel Vigo signed Apr. 17; Mikhail Pocknett, Kyle Jones and Omar Migues-Hibeljic were the main expected returners at the time of writing, with the roster still fluid.

previews.title: Pitt, Buffalo ready to prove preseason predictions wrong
previews.summary: Game preview ahead of Buffalo's Nov. 5 trip to Pitt. Notes Buffalo opened with a 92-65 loss at Marshall in which Tennessee State transfer Antoine Lorick had 28 points and 15 rebounds and Southern Illinois transfer Drew Steffe scored 19 in their Buffalo debuts. Outside those two the Bulls made 6 of 30 field goals and shot 5-of-27 (18.5%) from three. Halcovage praised his two top scorers and said the team must grow from the loss. Notes Buffalo has not made the NCAA Tournament since 2019.

previews.projected_finish: 10th (47 points, 0 first-place votes) in MAC preseason coaches poll
previews.summary: MAC preseason coaches poll released Oct. 20, 2026: Miami first (133 points, 9 first-place votes), Toledo, Akron, Kent State, Ohio, UMass, Bowling Green, Western Michigan, Eastern Michigan, Buffalo 10th (47), Ball State, Central Michigan 12th (25). storylines.headline: Complete roster turnover: no returning starters, top six scorers gone
storylines.detail: Freitag (Oregon State), Sabol (Providence), Brizzi, Oboh (Penn State), Batchelor and Talton Jr. all departed. Halcovage rebuilt with eight former D-I players plus D-III/NAIA additions.

storylines.headline: Former five-star J.J. Starling arrives from Syracuse
storylines.detail: Signed Sep. 4, 2026. 2022 McDonald's All-American; 1,530 career points at Notre Dame and Syracuse; averaged 17.8 PPG in 2024-25. Ranked No. 27 by ESPN as a recruit. A Heavy.com piece questions how he had eligibility remaining (not retrieved).

storylines.headline: Rough start: 0-2 with lopsided losses at Marshall and Pitt
storylines.detail: Lost 92-65 at Marshall (Nov. 2) and 80-61 at Pitt (Nov. 5) after leading by 15 early in the second half; outrebounded 50-27 at Pitt. Three-point shooting (5-of-27 at Marshall) and depth scoring were the issues in the opener.

storylines.headline: Halcovage year four: extended through 2029-30, expectations now 'compete for the MAC'
storylines.detail: Spectrum feature says the 4-27 to 17-15 jump was a 'proof of concept'; 716 Club launched with $500K; UB must replace Sabol and Freitag with transfers and development.

storylines.headline: Guard-heavy portal class built around Steffe, Tyne, Ducommun, Frakes
storylines.detail: April 27 release introduced four newcomers, all guards: SIU's Drew Steffe, Richmond's Mikkel Tyne, NIU's Dylan Ducommun and Oregon redshirt JJ Frakes; a second release Apr. 28 added two more veteran transfers (not retrieved).

players_in_coverage.name: J.J. Starling
players_in_coverage.notes: 6-4 guard from Baldwinsville, N.Y. 88 games at Syracuse: 13.8 PPG, 3.2 RPG, 2.3 APG; career-high 38 vs. Youngstown State; 17.8 PPG in 2024-25. 11.8 PPG in 28 games at Notre Dame. 1,530 career points. 2022 McDonald's All-American. sMACk Talk lists 10.9 PPG, 2.7 RPG, 2.4 APG for 2025-26. Eligibility status questioned by Heavy.com (not retrieved). At Pitt (Nov. 5): 13 points. Spectrum (Sep. 16) said he was awaiting a decision on fifth-year eligibility; he played vs. Pitt Nov. 5 (13 pts), indicating he was cleared.

recent_news.headline: Pitt rallies from 13 down at half to beat Buffalo 80-61; Ndongo 23 pts/21 reb
